claim: BMP4 and Nodal pathways share the signal transducer Smad4.
source: (a) BMP and Nodal pathways share the signal transducer Smad4.
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1a schematic diagram

claim: Each pathway (BMP4 and Nodal) has distinct receptor complexes that phosphorylate specific receptor-Smads.
source: Each pathway has distinct receptor complexes that phosphorylate specific signal transducers, known as receptor-Smads, which then complex with the shared cofactor Smad4 and translocate to the nucleus to activate target genes (Figure 1a) (Zinski et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zinski et al., 2018 and illustrated in Figure 1a

claim: A sudden increase in BMP4 leads to sustained SMAD4 signaling in hESCs.
source: We found that a sudden increase in BMP4 leads to sustained SMAD4 signaling (Figure 1b,d), consistent with our previous work (Nemashkalo et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1b,d and previous work citation

claim: The response to addition of Nodal and its substitute Activin is strongly adaptive (transient) and returns to a signaling baseline of around 20% of the response peak.
source: In contrast, the response to addition of Nodal and its substitute Activin is strongly adaptive, that is transient, and returns to a signaling baseline of around 20% of the response peak (Figure 1c,d, Figure 1—figure supplement 1i, j), similar to the previously observed response to TGFβ in C2C12 cells (Sorre et al., 2014; Warmflash et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by data in figures and comparison to previous work

claim: The response to recombinant Nodal was weak at all doses, likely reflecting the low quality of recombinant Nodal.
source: The response to recombinant Nodal was weak at all doses, likely reflecting the low quality of recombinant Nodal.
evidence: Based on experimental observation and speculation about protein quality

claim: To elicit a response in Nodal required 2 μg/ml of recombinant protein, whereas the response to Activin was saturated by 5 ng/ml.
source: To elicit a response in Nodal required 2 μg/ml of recombinant protein, whereas the response to Activin was saturated by 5 ng/ml (Figure 1f, Figure 1—figure supplement 1i, j).

claim: When the responses to Nodal and Activin were normalized to their respective maxima, their dynamics were identical.
source: However, when the responses to Nodal and Activin were normalized to their respective maxima, their dynamics were identical (Figure 1—figure supplement 1j).

claim: The peak and baseline signaling levels, but not the timescale of adaptation, depended on the Activin dose.
source: The peak and baseline signaling levels, but not the timescale of adaptation, depended on the Activin dose (Figure 1f).

claim: For BMP4, there was a sharp response so that even low doses gave a nearly full initial response.
source: For BMP4, there was a sharp response so that even low doses gave a nearly full initial response, however, the dose affected the duration of signaling in a way consistent with ligand depletion at low doses (Figure 1e, Appendix 1).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1e and explained by modeling in Appendix 1

claim: SMAD1/5/8 activation mirrors the SMAD4 response to BMP4.
source: Immunofluorescence staining for receptor-Smads revealed that SMAD1/5/8 activation mirrors the SMAD4 response to BMP4, while in response to Activin, SMAD2/3 nuclear localization adapts less than SMAD4 to about 60% of peak response (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e,g,h).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: In response to Activin, SMAD2/3 nuclear localization adapts less than SMAD4 to about 60% of peak response.
source: Immunofluorescence staining for receptor-Smads revealed that SMAD1/5/8 activation mirrors the SMAD4 response to BMP4, while in response to Activin, SMAD2/3 nuclear localization adapts less than SMAD4 to about 60% of peak response (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e,g,h).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: Addition of the BMP inhibitor Noggin had no effect on the dynamics in response to Activin.
source: In each case, the response was due to the added ligand and not to induced secondary signaling through the other pathway, as addition of the BMP inhibitor Noggin had no effect on the dynamics in response to Activin, while addition of the Activin inhibitor SB431542 slightly increased the response to BMP (Figure 1g,h).

claim: Addition of the Activin inhibitor SB431542 slightly increased the response to BMP.
source: In each case, the response was due to the added ligand and not to induced secondary signaling through the other pathway, as addition of the BMP inhibitor Noggin had no effect on the dynamics in response to Activin, while addition of the Activin inhibitor SB431542 slightly increased the response to BMP (Figure 1g,h).

claim: Endogenous BMP has no effect on the Nodal response.
source: Thus, endogenous BMP has no effect on the Nodal response, while Nodal signaling has a repressive effect on BMP.
evidence: Inferred from inhibitor experiments shown in Figure 1g,h

claim: Nodal signaling has a repressive effect on BMP.
source: Thus, endogenous BMP has no effect on the Nodal response, while Nodal signaling has a repressive effect on BMP.
evidence: Inferred from inhibitor experiments shown in Figure 1g,h

claim: Recovery on a timescale of minutes following nuclear photobleaching was observed in all cases, confirming that SMAD4 continuously shuttles between the nucleus and cytoplasm even in the absence of ligand stimulation.
source: In all cases, we observed recovery on a timescale of minutes following nuclear photobleaching, which confirmed that SMAD4 continuously shuttles between the nucleus and cytoplasm even in the absence of ligand stimulation (Figure 2d).

claim: A reduced recovery rate was observed after 1 hr of Activin treatment, consistent with previous work suggesting that nuclear accumulation of SMAD4 is caused by reduced nuclear export.
source: We also observed a reduced recovery rate after 1 hr of Activin treatment, consistent with previous work on TGFβ signaling which suggested that nuclear accumulation of SMAD4 is caused by reduced nuclear export (Nicolás et al., 2004; Schmierer and Hill, 2005).
evidence: FRAP data and comparison to previous work

claim: The recovery rate is not restored during adaptation.
source: Importantly, however, we found that the recovery rate is not restored during adaptation (Figure 2d), showing that cells do not revert to a pre-signaling state.

claim: Cells do not revert to a pre-signaling state during adaptation.
source: Importantly, however, we found that the recovery rate is not restored during adaptation (Figure 2d), showing that cells do not revert to a pre-signaling state.
evidence: Inferred from FRAP data showing recovery rate remains reduced

claim: The FRAP data and mathematical modeling exclude upstream mechanisms of adaptation as might be caused by secretion of extracellular feedback inhibitors or depletion of receptors or R-Smads.
source: This excludes upstream mechanisms of adaptation as might be caused by secretion of extracellular feedback inhibitors or depletion of receptors or R-Smads (Vizán et al., 2013).
evidence: Inferred from FRAP data and modeling

claim: If adaptation is caused by depletion of an upstream component such as receptors, then the magnitude of adaptation is governed by the ratio of the degradation rates of active and inactive receptors.
source: Moreover, mathematical modeling showed that if adaptation is caused by depletion of an upstream component such as receptors, then the magnitude of adaptation is governed by the ratio of the degradation rates of active and inactive receptors (Appendix 1).

claim: Models with negative feedback causing inhibition of downstream signaling are capable of explaining all features of the data including the observed time scales.
source: In contrast, models with negative feedback causing inhibition of downstream signaling are capable of explaining all features of our data including the observed time scales (Appendix 1).

claim: The nuclear to cytoplasmic intensity ratio systematically decreases after nuclear bleaching.
source: However, we observed that this ratio systematically decreases after nuclear bleaching (Figure 2f).

claim: A model that includes sequestered SMAD4 populations explains the systematic decrease in nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio after bleaching.
source: This suggests a more general model that includes sequestered SMAD4, which may move within but not between the nuclear and cytoplasmic compartments.
evidence: Inferred from FRAP data and explained by modeling

claim: Initial accumulation of SMAD4 in the nucleus reflects both a lower export rate and a reduction in cytoplasmic sequestration.
source: The parameters obtained from fitting this model to our data suggest that initial accumulation of SMAD4 in the nucleus reflects both a lower export rate and a reduction in cytoplasmic sequestration (Figure 2i,j).
evidence: Model fitting to FRAP data shown in Figure 2i,j

claim: Adaptation does not result from altering shuttling kinetics, but instead reflects reduced nuclear sequestration and increased cytoplasmic sequestration.
source: Adaptation, however, does not result from altering shuttling kinetics, but instead reflects reduced nuclear sequestration and increased cytoplasmic sequestration.
evidence: Model fitting to FRAP data shown in Figure 2i,j

claim: BMP targets are stably induced.
source: Next, we evaluated transcriptional dynamics downstream of BMP4 and Activin using qPCR, which showed that BMP targets are stably induced (Figure 3a), while differentiation targets of Nodal show adaptive transcription on a timescale consistent with SMAD4 signaling (Figure 3b).

claim: Differentiation targets of Nodal show adaptive transcription on a timescale consistent with SMAD4 signaling.
source: Next, we evaluated transcriptional dynamics downstream of BMP4 and Activin using qPCR, which showed that BMP targets are stably induced (Figure 3a), while differentiation targets of Nodal show adaptive transcription on a timescale consistent with SMAD4 signaling (Figure 3b).

claim: Shared targets of the BMP4 and Activin pathways were found to be transcribed adaptively in response to Activin and stably in response to BMP4.
source: Moreover, shared targets of the pathways were found to be transcribed adaptively in response to Activin and stably in response to BMP4 (Figure 3c, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: qPCR data shown in Figure 3c and Figure 3—figure supplement 1a

claim: The transcription of NODAL, WNT3, and their inhibitors LEFTY1 and CER1 were sustained upon Activin treatment.
source: In contrast, the transcription of NODAL, WNT3, and their inhibitors LEFTY1 and CER1 were sustained upon Activin treatment (Figure 3d).

claim: The differences in expression of these sets of targets are not due to differences in mRNA stability as mRNAs for stably expressed genes were found to decline rapidly upon pathway inhibition with SB431542.
source: The differences in expression of these sets of targets are not due to differences in mRNA stability as mRNAs for stably expressed genes were found to decline rapidly upon pathway inhibition with SB431542 indicating a need for ongoing signaling to maintain expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1g).

claim: BMP4 signaling responses to the ramp and step approached each other as ramp concentration increased.
source: As expected, BMP4 signaling responses to the ramp and step approached each other as ramp concentration increased, while Activin signaling was dramatically reduced in the case of the ramp (Figure 4b,e).

claim: Activin signaling was dramatically reduced in the case of the ramp compared to the step.
source: As expected, BMP4 signaling responses to the ramp and step approached each other as ramp concentration increased, while Activin signaling was dramatically reduced in the case of the ramp (Figure 4b,e).

claim: Transcriptional dynamics of the shared target HAND1 matched the signaling pattern and showed dramatically reduced transcription in response to the Activin but not the BMP ramp.
source: Moreover, transcriptional dynamics of the shared target HAND1 matched the signaling pattern and showed dramatically reduced transcription in response to the Activin but not the BMP ramp (Figure 4c,f).

claim: Intermediate rates of Activin increase yielded intermediate signaling responses.
source: Finally, we varied the rate of the ramp of Activin and found that intermediate rates of increase also yielded intermediate signaling responses (Figure 4g,h).

claim: Each pulse of Activin elicited a strong response in the translocation of SMAD4 to the cell nucleus.
source: Each pulse of Activin elicited a strong response in the translocation of SMAD4 to the cell nucleus, while no such responses were seen in response to the dummy pulses (Figure 5b).

claim: Differentiation to mesendoderm as marked by Bra expression was enhanced under pulsed Activin conditions, despite the reduced integrated ligand exposure.
source: Differentiation to mesendooderm as marked by Bra expression was also enhanced under pulsed conditions (Figure 5c,d), despite the reduced integrated ligand exposure.

claim: The effect of pulses is specific to pulsed Activin and not a consequence of simply reducing the integrated Activin exposure.
source: Continuous exposure to lower doses of Activin and treating cells with Activin for the same total time as the three pulses but in a single pulse showed that the effect is specific to pulsed Activin and not a consequence of simply reducing the integrated Activin exposure (Figure 5e–g, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Control experiments shown in Figure 5e–g and Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: Nodal signaling is required for the formation of mesoderm and endoderm within micropatterned colonies.
source: Nodal signaling is required for the formation of mesoderm and endoderm within these colonies, and both small molecule inhibition and genetic knockout of Nodal drastically reduce mesendoderm differentiation (Chhabra et al., 2018; Warmflash et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: The cells initially respond uniformly to the BMP4 treatment in micropatterned colonies.
source: The cells initially respond uniformly to the BMP4 treatment.
evidence: Observed in live imaging data shown in Figure 6a,b

claim: The BMP4 response is restricted to the colony edge by approximately 12 hr and this pattern is maintained until approximately 25 hr.
source: The response then is restricted to the colony edge by approximately 12 hr (Figure 6a,b), and this pattern is maintained until approximately 25 hr.
evidence: Live imaging data shown in Figure 6a,b

claim: Beginning at 25 hr, a wave of increased nuclear SMAD4 spreads inward again from the edge.
source: Beginning at 25 hr, a wave of increased nuclear SMAD4 spreads inward again from the edge (Figure 6a,c).
evidence: Live imaging data shown in Figure 6a,c

claim: The stable response at the edge of the colony represents BMP signaling while the inward moving wave results from Nodal signaling.
source: SMAD4 convolves the BMP and Nodal responses, and we hypothesized that the stable response at the edge of the colony represents BMP signaling while the inward moving wave results from Nodal signaling.
evidence: Hypothesis tested with pathway-specific SMAD staining

claim: The BMP-specific active SMAD1 signaling remains restricted to the edge.
source: These confirmed that the BMP-specific active SMAD1 signaling remains restricted to the edge (Figure 6f), while the Nodal transducer SMAD2/3 activity spreads rapidly inward from the colony edge between 24 and 36 hr (Figure 6e).

claim: The Nodal transducer SMAD2/3 activity spreads rapidly inward from the colony edge between 24 and 36 hr.
source: These confirmed that the BMP-specific active SMAD1 signaling remains restricted to the edge (Figure 6f), while the Nodal transducer SMAD2/3 activity spreads rapidly inward from the colony edge between 24 and 36 hr (Figure 6e).

claim: The SMAD2/3 and SMAD4 signal transducers reveal a rapidly evolving Nodal distribution with a wavefront that moves through the colony at approximately one-cell diameter (10 μm) per hour.
source: The SMAD2/3 and SMAD4 signal transducers reveal a rapidly evolving Nodal distribution with a wavefront that moves through the colony at approximately one-cell diameter (10 μm) per hour.
evidence: Calculated from data shown in Figure 6e and Figure 6a

claim: The wave of Nodal signaling activates Bra expression in its wake.
source: Importantly, this wave of signaling activates Bra expression in its wake (Figure 6g,h).

claim: Rapid increases in endogenous Nodal signaling are associated with mesoderm differentiation in this model of human gastrulation.
source: This indicates that rapid increases in endogenous Nodal signaling are associated with mesoderm differentiation in this model of human gastrulation.
evidence: Inferred from correlation between Nodal wave and Bra expression

claim: Morphogens in the mammalian embryo do not act in a purely concentration-dependent manner.
source: Our work shows that morphogens in the mammalian embryo do not act in a purely concentration-dependent matter and has revealed an important role for Activin/Nodal rate of change in specifying cell fate as a consequence of adaptive signaling.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from all experimental data presented

claim: There is an important role for Activin/Nodal rate of change in specifying cell fate as a consequence of adaptive signaling.
source: Our work shows that morphogens in the mammalian embryo do not act in a purely concentration-dependent matter and has revealed an important role for Activin/Nodal rate of change in specifying cell fate as a consequence of adaptive signaling.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from all experimental data presented

claim: Adaptive signaling could serve to restrict the response to a narrow competence window.
source: Adaptive signaling could serve to restrict the response to a narrow competence window or to separate the multiple roles of a single morphogen by using distinct dynamics to selectively activate different target genes, effectively expanding the information content of the morphogen gradient (Selimkhanov et al., 2014).
evidence: Speculation about functional significance with citation

claim: Adaptive signaling could separate the multiple roles of a single morphogen by using distinct dynamics to selectively activate different target genes, effectively expanding the information content of the morphogen gradient.
source: Adaptive signaling could serve to restrict the response to a narrow competence window or to separate the multiple roles of a single morphogen by using distinct dynamics to selectively activate different target genes, effectively expanding the information content of the morphogen gradient (Selimkhanov et al., 2014).
evidence: Speculation about functional significance with citation

claim: Micropatterned colonies of hESCs treated with BMP4 differentiate in a spatial pattern with reproducible rings of extraembryonic cells and all three germ layers.
source: These colonies differentiate in a spatial pattern with reproducible rings of extraembryonic cells and all three germ layers, and represent a model for the patterning associated with gastrulation in the human embryo (Heemskerk and Warmflash, 2016; Warmflash et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: Micropatterned colonies represent a model for the patterning associated with gastrulation in the human embryo.
source: These colonies differentiate in a spatial pattern with reproducible rings of extraembryonic cells and all three germ layers, and represent a model for the patterning associated with gastrulation in the human embryo (Heemskerk and Warmflash, 2016; Warmflash et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: In the vertebrate embryo, expression patterns of morphogens change rapidly, simultaneous with large-scale cell movements.
source: However, in the vertebrate embryo, expression patterns of these morphogens change rapidly, simultaneous with large-scale cell movements, and therefore individual cells experience substantial changes in morphogen levels during differentiation (Arnold and Robertson, 2009; Balaskas et al., 2012; Dessaud et al., 2007; Dubrulle et al., 2015; Kinder et al., 2001; van Boxtel et al., 2015).

claim: Individual cells experience substantial changes in morphogen levels during differentiation.
source: However, in the vertebrate embryo, expression patterns of these morphogens change rapidly, simultaneous with large-scale cell movements, and therefore individual cells experience substantial changes in morphogen levels during differentiation (Arnold and Robertson, 2009; Balaskas et al., 2012; Dessaud et al., 2007; Dubrulle et al., 2015; Kinder et al., 2001; van Boxtel et al., 2015).

claim: Duration of ligand exposure is a relevant parameter in cell fate decisions.
source: Duration of ligand exposure must logically be a relevant parameter, as was confirmed in a number of contexts, including Activin/Nodal signaling in early Zebrafish development and Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) signaling in the mouse neural tube (Dessaud et al., 2007; Sako et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: Nodal and BMP4 are morphogens crucial for gastrulation in vertebrates.
source: Nodal and BMP4 are morphogens crucial for gastrulation in vertebrates (Winnier et al., 1995).

claim: In the early mammalian embryo, BMP4 is required for both initiating gastrulation and specifying the dorsal-ventral axis.
source: In the early mammalian embryo, BMP4 is required for both initiating gastrulation and specifying the dorsal-ventral axis, while Nodal maintains the pluripotent epiblast and is subsequently required for mesoderm and endoderm differentiation (Conlon et al., 1994).

claim: Nodal maintains the pluripotent epiblast and is subsequently required for mesoderm and endoderm differentiation.
source: In the early mammalian embryo, BMP4 is required for both initiating gastrulation and specifying the dorsal-ventral axis, while Nodal maintains the pluripotent epiblast and is subsequently required for mesoderm and endoderm differentiation (Conlon et al., 1994).

claim: Both Nodal and BMP4 have been claimed to act in a concentration-dependent manner based on classic Xenopus experiments.
source: Both Nodal and BMP4 have been claimed to act in a concentration-dependent manner based on classic Xenopus experiments (Green et al., 1992; Gurdon et al., 1994; Wilson et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citations to classic experiments

claim: The classic Xenopus experiments allow alternative interpretations.
source: However, those experiments allow alternative interpretations (Heemskerk and Warmflash, 2016), and the role of BMP4 and Nodal ligand dynamics has not been investigated.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous analysis

claim: The role of BMP4 and Nodal ligand dynamics has not been investigated prior to this study.
source: However, those experiments allow alternative interpretations (Heemskerk and Warmflash, 2016), and the role of BMP4 and Nodal ligand dynamics has not been investigated.

claim: When hESCs are grown sparsely, their response to exogenous signals is uniform and not dependent on secondary signals.
source: Further, in contrast to the micropatterned colonies, when hESCs are grown more sparsely, their response to exogenous signals is uniform and not dependent on secondary signals, allowing for dissection of the dynamics of response (Nemashkalo et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Activin and Nodal are generally thought of as text-book morphogens acting in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: Activin and Nodal are generally thought of as text-book morphogens acting in a concentration-dependent manner (Gilbert, 2014).

claim: The patterning of the neural tube by Shh has been shown to be adaptive and regulates cell fate decisions through a described gene regulatory network.
source: Our results are in contrast to those for another well-characterized system, the patterning of the neural tube by Shh, which has also been shown to be adaptive and regulates cell fate decisions through a described gene regulatory network (Balaskas et al., 2012).

claim: In the Shh neural tube patterning system, adaptation depends on upstream inhibition and results in a relatively constant integrated signaling output in which time and duration can be interchanged.
source: In that case, adaptation depends on upstream inhibition and results in a relatively constant integrated signaling output in which time and duration can be interchanged (Dessaud et al., 2007).

claim: Blocking nuclear export of Smad4 does not interfere with function of the pathway.
source: Although it was shown that blocking nuclear export of Smad4 does not interfere with function of the pathway (Biondi et al., 2007), this does not invalidate our conclusions, as blocking nuclear export of Smad4 destroys the strong correlation between pathway activity and nuclear localization by artificially keeping Smad4 in the nucleus following the termination of transcription.

claim: Adaptive signaling is a common feature of biological systems.
source: Although relatively unexplored in the context of development, adaptive signaling is a common feature of biological systems.

claim: In bacterial chemotaxis, adaptive signaling allows cells to sense the rate of change and move to areas of higher nutrients.
source: Well-studied examples in bacteria include the chemotactic response where adaptive signaling allows cells to sense the rate of change and move to areas of higher nutrients (Block et al., 1983), and the σb response where it allows cells to sense the rate of increase of environmental stress (Young et al., 2013).

claim: In the bacterial σb response, adaptive signaling allows cells to sense the rate of increase of environmental stress.
source: Well-studied examples in bacteria include the chemotactic response where adaptive signaling allows cells to sense the rate of change and move to areas of higher nutrients (Block et al., 1983), and the σb response where it allows cells to sense the rate of increase of environmental stress (Young et al., 2013).

claim: Stimulation with TNFα leads to a transient pulse of NFκB signaling, followed by a low, sustained baseline.
source: In mammalian cells, stimulation with TNFα leads to a transient pulse of NFκB signaling, followed by a low, sustained baseline, and this has been suggested to allow specificity in target gene activation with different targets responding to different features of the dynamics (Hoffmann et al., 2002).

claim: DNA damage gives rise to stereotyped pulses of p53 signaling due to negative feedback.
source: Similarly, DNA damage has been shown to give rise to stereotyped pulses of p53 signaling due to negative feedback (Lahav et al., 2004).

claim: Current protocols for directed stem cell differentiation typically perform a single media change per day and do not take advantage of potential enhancements resulting from optimizing ligand dynamics.
source: It will be important to understand how our results fit with current protocols for directed stem cell differentiation which typically perform a single media change per day and therefore do not take advantage of potential enhancements resulting from optimizing ligand dynamics.

claim: The results will serve as a basis for a dynamic understanding of embryonic patterning and stem cell differentiation.
source: As such, we believe the results presented here will serve as a basis for a dynamic understanding of embryonic patterning and stem cell differentiation.
